| same detector/quality top query | 5917 | 0.5339 / 0.4112 | 0.5339 / 0.4112 | 0.5339 / 0.4112 | 0.5339 / 0.4112 | 0.0000 |
| different detector/quality top query | 3591 | 0.5567 / 0.4400 | 0.5341 / 0.3979 | 0.5450 / 0.4341 | 0.6054 / 0.4946 | 0.1273 |

Interpretation:

- Most rows (`5917 / 9508`) have no source-choice headroom because detector and
  quality select the same query.
- The useful headroom is concentrated in the `3591` different-query rows:
  detector-only is already `0.5567 / 0.4400`, but perfect detector-vs-quality
  choice would reach `0.6054 / 0.4946` on that subset.
- Current selection on different-query rows is below detector-only
  (`0.5450 / 0.4341` versus `0.5567 / 0.4400`) because quality overrides are
  too noisy.

Selector error categories over all rows:

| category | rows | ratio |
|---|---:|---:|
| missed quality when quality IoU is better | 856 | 0.0900 |
| selected quality when quality IoU is not better | 326 | 0.0343 |
| selected quality when quality IoU is better | 131 | 0.0138 |
| false quality override at Acc@0.25 threshold | 131 | 0.0138 |
| true quality override at Acc@0.25 threshold | 89 | 0.0094 |
| false keep-detector at Acc@0.25 threshold | 86 | 0.0090 |

Important feature bucket:

- In the highest quality-logit-margin quartile on different-query rows, the
  selector chooses quality on `0.5089` of samples, but detector/quality are both
  weak (`0.3174 / 0.1849` and `0.2539 / 0.1448`). This is the main false
  override pattern.
- In the lowest quality-logit-margin quartile, detector is very strong
  (`0.8073 / 0.7584`) and the selector correctly never chooses quality, but
  that bucket contains almost no deployable gain.
- Large detector-quality center deltas contain high oracle headroom
  (`0.5045 / 0.3374` in the largest-delta quartile) but also high quality harm;
  geometry disagreement is useful only if paired with a better source-choice
  objective.

Objective design note for the next code change:

- The existing `iou_aux` branch is not enough for the two-source
  `detector_jointtight,quality` setup because it ranks non-default sources
  against other non-default sources. With only one non-default source
  (`quality`), that auxiliary has no real competitor and should be treated as
  inactive for this branch.
- The needed objective is a bidirectional quality-vs-default margin trained only
  with GT IoU:
  - if `quality_top_iou >= detector_top_iou + gap`, require
    `quality_logit - detector_logit >= margin`;
  - if `detector_top_iou >= quality_top_iou + gap`, require
    `detector_logit - quality_logit >= margin`;
  - if the IoU gap is small or the two sources pick the same query, do not add
    this auxiliary pressure.
- This differs from the existing positive-only `quality_default_margin`: it
  also penalizes harmful quality overrides directly, which targets Run314's
  main failure mode.
- Proposed implementation should add parser/loss diagnostics and TDD coverage
  before any training launch. If implemented, the first experiment should be a
  one-epoch Run315 from Run297 epoch89 with the Run314 cleaned augmentation
  flags, not a long run.

## Code update: bidirectional quality-default margin for two-source gate

Implemented the Run314 diagnostic follow-up as a training-only auxiliary loss.
This does not change validation/inference scoring by itself; it only adds GT IoU
supervision during training for the source-choice selector.

New options:

```text
--source_pool_selector_quality_default_bidirectional_margin_weight
--source_pool_selector_quality_default_bidirectional_margin
```

Behavior:

- active only when `quality` and the configured default source are both present;
- computes top-1 queries for `quality` and the default source;
- ignores same-query rows;
- ignores rows where the absolute GT IoU gap is below the configured source gap;
- if quality top-1 has higher GT IoU, requires
  `quality_logit - default_logit >= margin`;
- if default top-1 has higher GT IoU, requires
  `default_logit - quality_logit >= margin`.

Files changed:

- `models/losses.py`
  - added the bidirectional margin loss and diagnostics:
    `dbg_source_pool_selector_quality_default_bidirectional_margin_loss`,
    `dbg_source_pool_selector_quality_default_bidirectional_margin_weight`,
    `dbg_source_pool_selector_quality_default_bidirectional_margin`,
    `dbg_source_pool_selector_quality_default_bidirectional_margin_valid_ratio`,
    `dbg_source_pool_selector_quality_default_bidirectional_margin_score_gap`,
    and `dbg_source_pool_selector_quality_default_bidirectional_margin_iou_gap`.
- `main_utils.py`
  - parser support, validation, diagnostic key registration, and loss
    pass-through.
- `tests/test_source_pool_selector.py`
  - TDD coverage for bidirectional gradients and parser support.

### Run315 row-level follow-up

I compared the preserved Run314 and Run315 source-choice row dumps under the
same two-source `detector_jointtight,quality` interpretation.

Run314 versus Run315:

| metric | Run314 | Run315 | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| selected quality ratio | 0.0481 | 0.0479 | -0.0002 |
| oracle quality ratio | 0.1038 | 0.1038 | 0.0000 |
| selected Acc@0.25 | 0.5381 | 0.5379 | -0.0002 |
| selected Acc@0.50 | 0.4199 | 0.4195 | -0.0003 |
| false base ratio | 0.0900 | 0.0897 | -0.0003 |
| false override ratio | 0.0343 | 0.0338 | -0.0005 |
| quality logit-margin mean | -1.4555 | -0.7858 | +0.6696 |
| source choice changed rows | n/a | 52 / 9508 | 0.0055 |

The bidirectional auxiliary did move the selector logits: the average quality
logit margin increased by about `+0.67`. However, it barely changed the actual
argmax source choice. Only `52` rows changed selected source:

| changed direction | rows | before Acc@0.25/0.50 | after Acc@0.25/0.50 | mean Run315 IoU gap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| detector -> quality | 25 | 0.5200 / 0.4400 | 0.2400 / 0.2000 | -0.1752 |
| quality -> detector | 27 | 0.0741 / 0.0370 | 0.2593 / 0.1481 | -0.1276 |

So the few changed rows were mostly detector-favored; the net metric stayed
slightly negative. This argues against simply increasing the bidirectional
margin weight or training this exact objective longer.

I also checked whether existing non-GT dump features separate useful quality
overrides from harmful ones at Acc@0.25:

| group | rows |
|---|---:|
| differing detector/quality top query | 3591 |
| quality uniquely fixes Acc@0.25 | 175 |
| quality uniquely hurts Acc@0.25 | 256 |

The usable feature separation is weak. After ignoring constant/binary-count
artifacts, the best continuous features only reach rough AUC/separation around
`0.57-0.60`; examples include RAPF JS divergence, quality-vs-target-detector
score delta, detector/quality size delta, and seed-objectness rank. Simple
threshold probes on these features gave at most tiny detector-primary gains,
for example:

| rule probe | selected quality | Acc@0.25 | Acc@0.50 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| detector-primary baseline | 0.0000 | 0.5425 | 0.4221 |
| quality-vs-target-detector score >= 95th percentile | 0.0190 | 0.5424 | 0.4224 |
| quality-vs-target-detector score <= 2.5th percentile | 0.0095 | 0.5431 | 0.4228 |

Decision update:

- Stop this exact Run315 bidirectional-margin branch. It changes logits but not
  enough useful decisions, and the rows it changes do not carry meaningful
  positive utility.
- Do not spend another long run on simply increasing the bidirectional margin
  weight.
- Keep the cleaned augmentation policy for any future serious selector run,
  because it fixes confirmed augmentation exposure, but current evidence says
  the remaining gap is a source-quality separability problem rather than an
  augmentation switch problem.
- If continuing Route3, the next useful change should introduce a new evidence
  source or a different training target, not another scalar margin on the same
  `detector_jointtight,quality` logits.

## Run316 raw target-detector source-pool probe

After the Run315 row-level follow-up, I rechecked the older Run180/184 detector
policy lead. The report already explains the important denominator issue:
Run180/184's `0.5554 / 0.4412` was measured on the detector-diagnostic-available
subset, while the fair full-validation `detector_jointtight` primary source is
Run219 at about `0.5425 / 0.4221`. Therefore the next check was not another
direct `detector_jointtight` eval. Instead, I tested whether the raw
target-detector diagnostic sources in the saved row dumps provide a learnable
non-GT evidence source.

Artifact:

`/root/autodl-tmp/butd_logs/new_method_v2/tuning/run316_detector_raw_source_pool_probe_fast/metrics.json`

Inputs:

- Train rows:
  `/root/autodl-tmp/butd_logs/new_method_v2/tuning/route3_run303_noaug_train_selector_logit_dump_from_run297_epoch89/source_choice_rows_train_noaug.pt`
- Val rows:
  `/root/autodl-tmp/butd_logs/new_method_v2/tuning/route3_run300_selector_logit_dump_from_run297_epoch89/source_choice_rows.pt`
- Features: `620` non-label, non-GT top-IoU columns after removing train-constant
  columns.
- Labels were recomputed per tested source pool from train top-IoU / threshold
  utility. GT IoU is used only to create train labels and to report validation
  metrics, not as an inference feature.

First observation: raw detector sources have high oracle headroom but weak
single-source performance.

| val source / oracle pool | Acc@0.25 | Acc@0.50 | source counts |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| always `detector_jointtight` | 0.5425 | 0.4221 | 9508 / 0 / 0 |
| always `target_detector` | 0.3992 | 0.3028 | 0 / 9508 / 0 |
| always `target_detector_logit` | 0.4638 | 0.3455 | 0 / 0 / 9508 |
| oracle over `detector_jointtight,target_detector,target_detector_logit` | 0.6164 | 0.4813 | 7329 / 1671 / 508 |

Train-to-val HGB probes did not convert that oracle headroom into a deployable
selector:

| pool / model | Acc@0.25 | Acc@0.50 | selected counts |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| detector-target pool, HGB lr0.03 | 0.5423 | 0.4199 | 8513 / 920 / 75 |
| detector-target pool, HGB lr0.02 | 0.5416 | 0.4200 | 8546 / 794 / 168 |
| full pool `base,quality,detector_jointtight,target_detector,target_detector_logit`, HGB lr0.03 | 0.5321 | 0.4114 | 6710 / 795 / 1122 / 787 / 94 |
| `contrastive_base` full pool, HGB lr0.03 | 0.5380 | 0.4159 | 6947 / 666 / 1092 / 722 / 81 |

Simple validation-only rule probes also failed to beat the detector-primary
baseline. The best rule was effectively no switch; switching to `target_detector`
under high-margin or high-semantic-confidence conditions reduced both metrics.

Decision:

- Do not launch a long learned selector run that simply adds
  `target_detector` / `target_detector_logit` as extra sources.
- The raw target-detector sources are useful as diagnostics and as an oracle
  explanation for remaining headroom, but current train-to-val evidence says
  their useful cases are not separable enough by the existing frozen row
  features.
- This reinforces the Run315 conclusion: the next productive change needs a new
  representation or training target, not another broader fixed source pool or
  post-hoc selector over the same features.

  `--spacy_relation_free_view_guard_aug`,
  `--spacy_relation_free_compass_guard_aug`, and
  `--spacy_direction_sensitive_no_jitter_aug`.

Training and validation confirmed the cleaned augmentation policy mechanically:

- train `dbg_data_augment_det_active_ratio=0.0000`;
- train `dbg_data_aug_box_jitter_active_ratio=0.0000`;
- train direction-sensitive jitter/color/noise/shift/scale/pitch-roll and
  detector-corruption ratios stayed at `0.0000`;
- validation point-cloud augmentation, box jitter, and detector augmentation
  stayed at `0.0000`.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| Run225 best metric reference | 0.5431 | 0.4226 | 0.3498 | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| current best loadable detector-primary | 0.5425 | 0.4221 | 0.3495 | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a |

Decision:

- Reject Run317 as a deployable checkpoint. It is below both Run225
  (`0.5431 / 0.4226`) and the loadable detector-primary baseline
  (`0.5425 / 0.4221`).
- Do not continue this exact full-fine-tune branch. Low-LR full-model training
  made some RAPF validation diagnostics positive, but the selector collapsed
  further toward detector default and did not convert oracle headroom into
  deployable source choices.
- The cleaned augmentation policy remains useful and should stay in serious
  selector runs, but Run317 reinforces the Route1 conclusion: augmentation
  noise is real and controlled, yet the remaining gap is not closed by
  augmentation cleanup plus low-LR fine-tuning.
- Low-score `ckpt_epoch_90.pth` and `ckpt_epoch_last.pth` were deleted after
  preserving `config.json`, `log.txt`, `eval_epoch_90.log`, and
  `eval_results_latest.json`. `/root/autodl-tmp` returned to about `13 GB`
  free.

Current best remains unchanged:

  (checkpoint missing);
- best loadable deployable metric: detector-primary `0.5425 / 0.4221`.

  the same source pools, or another scalar/threshold variant of these gates.

  productive experiment needs a new representation, not another post-hoc
  top1-source gate.

## Run323 text-derived target class replacement for target-detector diagnostics

Run323 audited whether the strong historical target-detector diagnostics can be
made deployable by replacing validation GT `target_cid` with a class inferred
from decomposed target text.

Code changes:

- `src/joint_det_dataset.py` now emits `text_target_cid` from `target_slot`
  text only. It intentionally does not use `object_name`, `object_id`,
  `target_id`, or the full description as fallback.
- `src/grounding_evaluator.py` honors
  `--eval_target_cid_source {gt,text}`. `text` uses `text_target_cid` and does
  not fall back to GT `target_cid`.
- `main_utils.py` and `train_dist_mod.py` forward `text_target_cid`.
- `models/bdetr.py` now applies the same source rule to deployable
  detector-policy primary score sources during eval. This closes a deployment
  boundary where `--eval_primary_score_source detector_*` could still build
  model-side detector-policy scores from GT `target_cid`.
- `src/grounding_evaluator.py` now records detector count-boost diagnostic
  variants on the full evaluated sample denominator. If detector class/conf
  prior scores are absent, the diagnostic falls back to pure `quality`; if the
  detector count itself is unavailable, the count boost is inactive but the
  sample is still recorded. This fixes the old conditional-denominator audit
  gap for `detector_count_boost_combo`,
  `detector_count_boost_le2_combo`, and
  `detector_count_boost_fine_combo`.

  diagnostics use quality fallback and keep the full denominator.

  apparent gain was an audit-metric side effect, not a deployable innovation.
  The current mapper remains a viable but noisy deployment bridge; the next
  useful step is either improve the target-slot class mapper for the
  high-frequency mismatch families or train a deployable selector/objective
  that beats the Run297 detector-primary reference under full-denominator eval.

  validation.

## Run325 actual-target text alias diagnostic

Run325 rechecked the text-target alias idea with the same target-class
definition used by `Joint3DDataset`: the ground-truth class id comes from the
scan object's instance label through `label_map`/`DC.nyu40id2class`, while the
predicted text class still comes only from deployable `target_slot` text. This
replaces the earlier rough `object_name`-based sanity check and matches the
Run323 dataset-summary denominator.

Artifact:

- `/root/autodl-tmp/butd_logs/new_method_v2/tuning/run325_text_target_alias_actual_cid_diagnostic/alias_actual_target_cid_summary.json`

Baseline text-target class quality was reproduced:

| split | total | valid | valid ratio | exact match total | exact match valid |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| train | 36665 | 36043 | 0.9830 | 0.8771 | 0.8922 |
| val | 9508 | 9324 | 0.9806 | 0.8703 | 0.8875 |

Train-derived alias remap candidates with the largest apparent gains:

| alias | current class | train majority | train gain / count | purity |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| `computer` | computer tower | monitor | 163 / 240 | 0.721 |
| `round table` | round table | table | 91 / 145 | 0.766 |
| `wardrobe` | closet | closet wardrobe | 64 / 72 | 0.889 |
| `sofa` | sofa | couch | 46 / 53 | 0.868 |
| `board` | board | whiteboard | 41 / 82 | 0.707 |
| `painting` | painting | picture | 29 / 39 | 0.872 |
| `can` | can | trash can | 24 / 34 | 0.824 |

Validation replay of candidate policies:

| policy | remaps | val fixed | val broken | val match total | val match valid |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| purity 0.85 / gain 10 / count 20 | `painting->picture`, `sofa->couch`, `wardrobe->closet wardrobe` | 27 | 0 | 0.8703 -> 0.8732 | 0.8875 -> 0.8904 |
| purity 0.80 / gain 20 / count 30 | above + `can->trash can` | 31 | 0 | 0.8703 -> 0.8736 | 0.8875 -> 0.8908 |
| purity 0.75 / gain 30 / count 50 | `round table->table`, `sofa->couch`, `wardrobe->closet wardrobe` | 43 | 0 | 0.8703 -> 0.8748 | 0.8875 -> 0.8921 |
| purity 0.70 / gain 30 / count 50 | above + `board->whiteboard`, `computer->monitor` | 131 | 3 | 0.8703 -> 0.8838 | 0.8875 -> 0.9012 |
| manual high-precision | `can->trash can`, `painting->picture`, `sofa->couch` | 23 | 0 | 0.8703 -> 0.8727 | 0.8875 -> 0.8900 |
| manual no-computer | high-precision + `board->whiteboard`, `round table->table` | 72 | 0 | 0.8703 -> 0.8779 | 0.8875 -> 0.8952 |

Decision:

- Do not hard-change the default text-target mapper yet. The conservative
  remaps improve only the intermediate `text_target_cid` match ratio by
  `+0.0024` to `+0.0045` absolute on validation, which is too small to assume
  an Acc gain without a full eval.
- The larger `computer->monitor` gain is not safe as a default rule. It fixes
  many monitor mentions but breaks real computer-tower examples such as
  "desk top computer hard drive tower" and generic "computer" references.
- The useful output of this branch is an audit target, not a confirmed metric
  innovation: if a future detector-policy eval is cheap, test only a
  configurable alias-remap mode and keep the original strict mapper as the
  default. Any reported metric must use full-denominator deployable eval with
  `--eval_target_cid_source text`, not GT `target_cid`.

## Run328/329 clean-augmentation diff-query source-choice probe

This probe tested whether the source-choice selector was being diluted by rows
where `detector_jointtight` and `quality` selected the same top query. Those
same-query rows have no source-choice headroom but were still training the
selector as keep-default negatives. A new target,
`threshold_gain_default_diffquery_sourcewise_focal_bce`, filters the supervised
selector rows to cases where at least one non-default source and the default
source choose different top queries.

Code changes:

- `models/losses.py`
  - tracks each source's top query for source-choice supervision;
  - adds `threshold_gain_default_diffquery_sourcewise_focal_bce`;
  - reports
    `dbg_source_pool_selector_choice_target_threshold_gain_default_diffquery_sourcewise_focal_bce`
    and `dbg_source_pool_selector_diffquery_valid_ratio`.
- `main_utils.py`
  - parser and validation allow the new choice target.
- `tests/test_source_pool_selector.py`
  - covers same-query keep-default filtering and parser support.

Run328 trained one epoch from the best loadable checkpoint while keeping the
clean augmentation policy:

- start checkpoint:
  `/root/autodl-tmp/butd_logs/new_method_v2/scanrefer/two_stage/297_candidateaware_3src_loosegap003_from_run261_epoch88_to_90_b112/scanrefer_spacy/1779169753/ckpt_epoch_89.pth`
- output:
  `/root/autodl-tmp/butd_logs/new_method_v2/scanrefer/two_stage/328_twosource_cleanaug_diffquery_noaugdet_from_run297_epoch89_to90_b112/scanrefer_spacy/1781036431`
- clean augmentation:
  `augment_det=False`, `disable_box_jitter=True`,
  `spacy_relation_free_yaw_only_aug=True`,
  `spacy_relation_free_view_guard_aug=True`,
  `spacy_relation_free_compass_guard_aug=True`,
  `spacy_direction_sensitive_no_jitter_aug=True`.

Important boundary: the original Run328 command did not include
`--eval_target_cid_source text`, so its built-in validation would have used GT
target class for detector-policy features. After `ckpt_epoch_90.pth` was saved,
the GT-target validation was stopped and the checkpoint was evaluated in a
separate deployable run with text-derived target class only.

Run328 train diagnostics showed that the augmentation guards were mechanically
active:

| step | augment-det | box jitter | direction-sensitive jitter/color/noise/shift/scale/pitch-roll/det-corrupt | diff-query valid | selector valid | selected quality | target quality |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 100 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.4865 | 0.3336 | 0.2461 | 0.0877 |
| 200 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.4921 | 0.3395 | 0.2446 | 0.0862 |
| 300 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.4890 | 0.3345 | 0.2381 | 0.0831 |
| 400 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.4966 | 0.3456 | 0.2083 | 0.0860 |

The mechanical result was good: `--augment_det` and box jitter were off, and

- The clean augmentation policy remains valid: no detector corruption, no box

- Because Run329 was below best, the temporary Run328 epoch90 checkpoint was
  deleted after preserving config, log, JSON results, and row dumps. Protected
  checkpoints were not touched.

### Run329 offline selector-gate replay

I replayed the preserved Run329 row dump to test whether a deployable
eval-time gate could fix the remaining `quality` false-overrides without
another training run:

`/root/autodl-tmp/butd_logs/new_method_v2/scanrefer/two_stage/329_eval_texttarget_from_run328_epoch90_b112/source_choice_rows.pt`

The dump has `9508` rows and records the actual source order:

```text
source_names = (
  detector_jointtight,
  quality,
  contrastive_base,
  target_detector,
  target_detector_logit,
)
selector_choice_source_names = (detector_jointtight, quality)
```

Two-source replay over `detector_jointtight,quality` reproduced the deployment
pattern:

| policy | Acc@0.25 | Acc@0.50 | selected quality | IoU gap to oracle | mean IoU |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| raw Run329 selector | 0.5379 | 0.4181 | 0.1493 | 0.0151 | 0.3460 |
| always `detector_jointtight` | 0.5397 | 0.4205 | 0.0000 | 0.0137 | 0.3474 |
| always `quality` | 0.5340 | 0.4062 | 1.0000 | 0.0211 | 0.3399 |
| oracle `detector_jointtight,quality` | 0.5572 | 0.4389 | 0.0952 | 0.0000 | 0.3611 |

I then swept deployable scalar gates of the form
`quality_logit - detector_jointtight_logit > threshold`, plus simple gates
using non-GT row features such as same/different top query, parse confidence,
view dependency, relation-pair count, and decomposition status.

Best replayed gates:

| gate | threshold | Acc@0.25 | Acc@0.50 | selected quality | narrow false override | false base | mean IoU |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| parse confidence >= 0.8 | +0.62 | 0.5402 | 0.4210 | 0.0194 | 0.0050 | 0.0874 | 0.3479 |
| parse confidence >= 0.8 | +0.65 | 0.5404 | 0.4209 | 0.0187 | 0.0048 | 0.0877 | 0.3480 |
| view-dependent only | +0.36 | 0.5404 | 0.4207 | 0.0281 | 0.0080 | 0.0855 | 0.3478 |
| high global margin, no extra feature gate | about +2.0 | 0.5397 | 0.4206 | about 0.003 | about 0.0005 | about 0.094 | 0.3474 |

Here `narrow false override` means selecting `quality` when
`detector_jointtight_top_iou > quality_top_iou`. This is different from the
evaluator's override-vs-default diagnostic, where any non-default selection is
counted as an override and `false override` means the oracle source is the
default. Both views agree on the same conclusion: Run329 over-selects quality,
and making the gate conservative mostly collapses back to detector-primary.

The same row dump shows that the larger headroom is not in another scalar
two-source threshold. It is in choosing among more evidence sources, but that
is diagnostic headroom until a deployable selector can learn it:

| source / oracle pool | Acc@0.25 | Acc@0.50 | mean IoU |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| always `detector_jointtight` | 0.5397 | 0.4205 | 0.3474 |
| always `quality` | 0.5340 | 0.4062 | 0.3399 |
| always `contrastive_base` | 0.5297 | 0.4030 | 0.3403 |
| always `target_detector` | 0.3573 | 0.2725 | 0.2305 |
| always `target_detector_logit` | 0.4268 | 0.3180 | 0.2742 |
| oracle over all dumped sources | 0.6329 | 0.5068 | 0.4197 |
| oracle `detector_jointtight,quality,target_detector_logit` | 0.6210 | 0.4911 | 0.4071 |
| oracle `detector_jointtight,quality,contrastive_base` | 0.5682 | 0.4556 | 0.3740 |

Oracle source mix over all dumped sources:

| source | oracle ratio |
|---|---:|
| `detector_jointtight` | 0.6272 |
| `quality` | 0.0695 |
| `contrastive_base` | 0.1181 |
| `target_detector` | 0.1333 |
| `target_detector_logit` | 0.0520 |

Bucket diagnosis using deployable row features:

| bucket | rows | raw selected quality | quality better than detector | quality worse than detector |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| all | 9508 | 0.1493 | 0.0952 | 0.1406 |
| different detector/quality query | 3300 | 0.2633 | 0.2742 | 0.4052 |
| same detector/quality query | 6208 | 0.0888 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| parse confidence >= 0.8 | 5366 | 0.1478 | 0.1066 | 0.1454 |
| parse confidence < 0.8 | 4142 | 0.1514 | 0.0804 | 0.1345 |

Decision:

- Do not implement or launch a long run for a simple Run329 eval-time
  two-source threshold. Its best replayed result, about `0.5404 / 0.4210`, is
  only a small recovery toward detector-primary and remains below Run297
  `0.5425 / 0.4221` and Run225 `0.5431 / 0.4226`.
- Do not treat the large all-source oracle as deployable progress. It uses GT
  IoU only for offline diagnosis and mainly shows that useful evidence exists
  in the dumped sources if a future model can learn when to trust them.
- The immediate Route1 conclusion is unchanged but sharper: clean
  augmentation removes confirmed side effects, while the remaining gap is
  source-choice separability. The next useful experiment should add a better
  source-choice representation or training signal, not another single
  augmentation toggle or scalar selector bias.

### Source-choice dump spaCy augmentation audit fields

While replaying Run329, I found a remaining audit gap: sharded
`source_choice_rows.pt` records decomposition context and source scores, but it
did not record the per-sample `spacy_rotation_mode_id` or
`spacy_augmentation_profile_id`. That meant the evaluator could print aggregate
`spacy_profile_*` buckets, but offline source-choice row analysis could not
cross-tab false overrides against the exact augmentation/profile bucket.

Code update:

- `src/grounding_evaluator.py`
  - `GroundingEvaluator._source_choice_context_features` now adds numeric
    source-choice row fields:
    `spacy_rotation_mode_id` and `spacy_augmentation_profile_id`;
  - adds numeric one-hot fields such as `spacy_aug_yaw_only`,
    `spacy_profile_yaw_relation_free`, and
    `spacy_profile_stable_direction_sensitive`;
  - syncs the evaluator profile-name mapping with the dataset mapping by adding
    profile id `11: stable_direction_sensitive`.
- `tests/test_source_pool_selector.py`
  - covers the new fields for both top-1 source-choice feature rows and
    top-k candidate rows.

This is audit-only. It does not change training labels, source-choice logits,
or validation scoring. Its purpose is to make the next row dump capable of
answering which decomposed-text augmentation/profile buckets are associated
with useful source switches versus false overrides.

| profile | rows | selected Acc@0.25 / Acc@0.50 | detector | base | quality | selector-source oracle | selected mix det/base/quality | strict non-detector better | useful / harmful / missed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| `spacy_profile_none` | 5035 | 0.5122 / 0.3972 | 0.5132 / 0.4006 | 0.4931 / 0.3714 | 0.5120 / 0.3885 | 0.5476 / 0.4361 | 0.900 / 0.099 / 0.000 | 0.203 | 0.023 / 0.025 / 0.177 |

| `spacy_profile_yaw_relation_free` | 1941 | 0.5528 / 0.4359 | 0.5616 / 0.4426 | 0.5353 / 0.4034 | 0.5456 / 0.4225 | 0.5945 / 0.4776 | 0.891 / 0.108 / 0.001 | 0.232 | 0.032 / 0.031 / 0.196 |
| `spacy_profile_stable_direction_sensitive` | 488 | 0.4447 / 0.3340 | 0.4488 / 0.3361 | 0.4262 / 0.3135 | 0.4426 / 0.3197 | 0.4775 / 0.3750 | 0.865 / 0.135 / 0.000 | 0.197 | 0.025 / 0.035 / 0.170 |

Interpretation:

- The new row fields are valid and make the Route1 audit actionable at the
  per-profile level.
- No spaCy augmentation/profile bucket prefers `base` or `quality` as a global
  deployable primary. `detector_jointtight` remains the best fixed source in
  every bucket.
- `spacy_profile_yaw_relation` and `spacy_profile_yaw_relation_free` remain
  strong buckets under the clean policy. They do not justify removing the
  guarded yaw-only relation-free route.
- `spacy_profile_stable_direction_sensitive` is the weakest bucket and has the
  highest harmful non-detector switch ratio, but validation has no active point
  cloud augmentation. This bucket is therefore best read as a hard
  direction-sensitive/view-compass subset, not proof that the no-jitter guard
  itself is harmful.
- The remaining headroom is source-choice separability: about `21.3%` of rows
  have a strict non-detector improvement over detector, but the selector takes
  a useful switch only `2.5%` of the time and misses strict opportunities on
  `18.5%` of rows.

Decision:

- Keep the clean Route1 augmentation policy and its diagnostics.
- Do not launch another single-toggle augmentation run from this evidence.
- Do not use `selector_choice` as a deployable improvement over detector-primary
  for this checkpoint; it is below the same-run detector fallback.
- The next useful Route1-adjacent experiment should improve the source-choice
  representation/objective for strict non-detector opportunities, especially in
  `yaw_relation_free` and `stable_direction_sensitive`, while preserving
  detector-primary as the fallback.

### Run331 offline source-choice separability replay

After Run331, I replayed the row dump with deployable row features only to test
whether the newly visible spaCy profile fields make useful source switches easy
to separate from harmful switches. This is an offline diagnostic on validation
rows, not a deployable metric and not a result to compare against Run225.

Reference labels:

- selector sources: `detector_jointtight,base,quality`;
- tie-pref oracle over selector sources:
  `0.5715 / 0.4575 / 0.3761`;
- detector fallback:
  `0.5397 / 0.4205 / 0.3474`;
- current selector:
  `0.5369 / 0.4171 / 0.3458`;
- strict tie-pref source counts:
  `detector_jointtight=7482`, `base=1640`, `quality=386`.

The strongest single deployable features for predicting a strict non-detector
opportunity were not the spaCy profile bits. They were source disagreement and
geometry features:

| feature | univariate AUC |
|---|---:|
| `source_pair_detector_jointtight_base_top_volume_abs_delta` | 0.7063 |
| `detector_jointtight_base_same_query` | 0.6977 |
| `source_pair_detector_jointtight_base_top_size_l1_delta` | 0.6972 |
| `detector_jointtight_contrastive_base_same_query` | 0.6928 |
| `source_pair_detector_jointtight_base_top_center_l1_delta` | 0.6716 |
| `source_pair_base_quality_top_volume_abs_delta` | 0.6705 |
| `source_pair_base_quality_top_size_l1_delta` | 0.6676 |
| `base_quality_same_query` | 0.6658 |
| `detector_jointtight_top_sem_cls_margin` | 0.6527 |
| `detector_jointtight_top_sem_cls_max` | 0.6498 |

Adding the new spaCy fields to this val-row feature analysis did not change the
top feature list or the balanced-logistic replay. The top-40 feature replay was
identical with and without spaCy fields:

| feature set | offline replay | selected detector/base/quality | useful | harmful | missed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| current features, no spaCy | 0.5302 / 0.4002 / 0.3377 | 0.361 / 0.415 / 0.224 | 0.180 | 0.231 | 0.007 |
| current features + spaCy | 0.5302 / 0.4002 / 0.3377 | 0.361 / 0.415 / 0.224 | 0.180 | 0.231 | 0.007 |

This explains the failure mode: the feature space can identify many strict
non-detector opportunities, but a balanced classifier over-selects base/quality
and hurts metric because harmful switches rise faster than useful switches.

I then replayed a conservative probability gate: default to
`detector_jointtight`, and switch to the best non-detector source only when the
cross-validated non-detector probability exceeds a threshold.

| feature set | threshold | offline replay | non-detector rate | useful | harmful | missed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| top-20 current + spaCy | 0.95 | 0.5392 / 0.4203 / 0.3472 | 0.002 | 0.000 | 0.001 | 0.213 |
| top-40 current + spaCy | 0.95 | 0.5394 / 0.4203 / 0.3472 | 0.002 | 0.000 | 0.001 | 0.212 |
| top-80 current + spaCy | 0.95 | 0.5392 / 0.4202 / 0.3471 | 0.003 | 0.001 | 0.001 | 0.212 |
| top-40 current + spaCy | 0.70 | 0.5384 / 0.4149 / 0.3451 | 0.201 | 0.064 | 0.082 | 0.144 |
| top-40 current + spaCy | 0.80 | 0.5386 / 0.4203 / 0.3467 | 0.058 | 0.017 | 0.025 | 0.194 |

Decision:

- Do not build another eval-time scalar/probability gate from Run331 rows. The
  conservative regime collapses back to detector-primary and still stays below
  the detector fallback, while lower thresholds over-select harmful switches.
- Adding spaCy profile fields to selector context is safe and may help profile
  specialization, but Run331 replay says it is not enough by itself.
- The useful training signal is source disagreement structure:
  same/different query, top-box geometry deltas, and detector semantic
  confidence. Future selector work should emphasize precision-first switching
  using these features rather than another augmentation toggle.

### Precision-first source-choice target for Run332

To turn the Run331 separability result into a trainable Route1-adjacent probe, I
added a new source-choice target:
`precision_gain_default_sourcewise_focal_bce`.

Design:

- default source remains `detector_jointtight`;
- a non-default source is supervised only when all of these are true:
  - the non-default top query differs from the detector top query;
  - its threshold bucket is strictly better than the detector bucket;
  - its top IoU exceeds detector top IoU by the configured
    `source_min_iou_gaps` value;
- sourcewise focal BCE is reused so the model still learns which non-default
  source to trust after the binary override decision;
- this is intentionally stricter than
  `threshold_gain_default_diffquery_sourcewise_focal_bce`, which reduced
  same-query dilution but still over-selected quality in Run329.

Code update:

- `models/losses.py`
  - accepts `precision_gain_default_sourcewise_focal_bce`;
  - adds the precision-first mask described above;
  - reports
    `dbg_source_pool_selector_choice_target_precision_gain_default_sourcewise_focal_bce`;
- `main_utils.py`
  - parser and source-choice validation accept the new target;
  - diagnostic logging includes the new debug key;
- `tests/test_source_pool_selector.py`
  - covers the low-margin cross-threshold case that must keep detector;
  - covers the high-margin cross-threshold case that must train a quality
    override;
  - covers parser support.
